title: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment
gist: Apple researchers derive the information-theoretic maximum expected reward gain for KL-regularized LM alignment (governed by a Jeffreys divergence term, not √KL), show reward hacking grows with reward error and lower KL penalty, prove reward ensembling mitigates it, and find best-of-N nears the limit while PPO and GRPO remain substantially suboptimal.

insights.claim: Apple researchers derived a closed-form expression for the maximum expected reward improvement achievable under a fixed KL-divergence budget in language model alignment, governed by a Jeffreys divergence term rather than the √KL used in prior analyses.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Gives a theoretical ceiling for how much alignment can improve a base model, useful for judging alignment-method claims.
insights.quote: governed by a Jeffreys divergence term rather than the √KL√KL√KL used in prior analyses
insights.locator: Our first result provides a closed-form

insights.claim: The optimal alignment reward gain can be reformulated as a covariance under the base model, yielding a practical estimator that predicts achievable alignment gains from base model samples alone.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Labs could forecast alignment ROI before spending on RL post-training compute.
insights.quote: yielding a practical estimator that predicts achievable alignment gains from base model samples alone

insights.claim: Despite widespread use of RL and best-of-N alignment, the fundamental limits of reward improvement under a KL budget had remained poorly understood.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Alignment spend has been largely empirical; theory may reallocate post-training budgets.

insights.claim: In proxy-reward alignment, the gap between ideal and proxy alignment (reward hacking) grows with the magnitude of reward error and as the KL penalty factor decreases.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Aggressive optimization against imperfect reward models carries quantifiable quality and safety risk.

insights.claim: Reward ensembling provably mitigates reward hacking, giving theoretical justification for a technique already used in practice.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Supports investment in multiple reward models as a robustness practice in post-training pipelines.

insights.claim: On safety and summarization tasks, best-of-N alignment closely approaches the theoretical KL–reward Pareto frontier, while PPO and GRPO remain substantially suboptimal.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Widely used RL algorithms leave measurable alignment gains on the table, an opening for better post-training methods.

insights.claim: Because best-of-N achieves near-optimal alignment only at high inference cost, algorithmic improvements are needed to reach optimal alignment without those costs.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Training-time alignment methods that match best-of-N would reduce inference compute bills; a likely research and product race.
